audit_findings.title: Missile Solutions subsidiary preferred creates a numerator-denominator claim mismatch
audit_findings.magnitude: $1,422m filed redemption amount; $968m mezzanine carrying value; $130m conversion-feature liability; $186m warrant liability; approximately 10% expected subsidiary ownership plus 3% warrants
audit_findings.mechanism: The DCF capitalizes consolidated Missile Solutions OE and divides by LHX common shares while omitting the subsidiary preferred claim, conversion dilution and warrants; the bridge also adds $1,521m of cash after receipt of $973m net preferred proceeds.
audit_findings.evidence: Pursuant to the terms of the proposed transaction, the DoW has agreed to be the anchor investor through a $ 1.0 billion convertible preferred security.
audit_findings.explanation: This is a demonstrated claim mismatch, not merely a possible future issue. The preferred was issued on April 17, 2026, and ranks ahead of LHX common through redemption, cumulative dividends or conversion. Its $1,422m redemption amount equals 4.0% of the $35,236m base equity value before considering the potentially larger effect of subsidiary dilution. Adding the financed cash while assigning all subsidiary earnings to LHX common can double-count value.
audit_findings.action: Rerun the valuation using Missile Solutions OE attributable to LHX common under each IPO, non-IPO redemption and sale scenario; recognize the preferred and warrant claims consistently, restrict transaction proceeds to their required investment use, and prevent those proceeds from being counted twice.

audit_findings.title: The null perimeter contradicts the announced Space Technology disposal
audit_findings.magnitude: $825m filed net enterprise value; 40% retained interest; $59m YTD 2026 pretax income; $1,010m assets and $113m liabilities held for sale
audit_findings.mechanism: Closing removes consolidated Space Technology operating earnings and assets, replacing them with cash proceeds, taxes and costs, and a 40% equity-method interest. A null perimeter continues the pre-closing business within OE without separately recognizing the post-closing consideration and retained claim.
audit_findings.evidence: Under the agreement we will contribute certain of the assets and liabilities of the SPPS business, reported in our AR segment, and the SA&C business, reported in our IMS segment to a new entity in which we will retain a 40 % noncontrolling interest.
audit_findings.explanation: The signed disposal and held-for-sale classification demonstrate that the valuation perimeter is incomplete. The record through July 30, 2026 says closing was expected early in the second half, but does not establish its status on September 5. Direction is mixed because removing full earnings lowers operating value while proceeds and the retained interest add value. The filed transaction and earnings amounts are large enough to require a rerun before relying on the valuation.
audit_findings.action: Establish closing status as of September 5, 2026, then rerun on the correct perimeter: remove post-closing OE, add net cash proceeds after taxes and costs, separately value the 40% retained interest, and reconcile the $59m YTD earnings and held-for-sale balances.

audit_findings.title: Non-operating pension income may be embedded in owner earnings
audit_findings.magnitude: $356m FY2025 pretax non-service pension income and $150m YTD 2026 pretax
audit_findings.mechanism: Net-income-based OE includes expected pension-asset returns, actuarial amortization and settlement effects unless explicitly removed; capitalizing that income increases the OE anchor and every scenario's operating and terminal value.
audit_findings.evidence: We record the service cost component of net periodic benefit income in the “Cost of revenue” and “General and administrative expenses” line items and the non-service cost components in the “Non-service FAS pension income and other, net” line item in our Consolidated Statement of Operations.
audit_findings.explanation: The filings demonstrate that non-service pension income is outside operating income, while the stated valuation method identifies only portfolio interest income as purged. The filed amounts are 14.8% and 6.3% of the $2,399.6m anchor, respectively, before tax and period alignment. That scale is reasonably capable of materially changing the DCF. The exact after-tax OE error remains unestablished until the calculation is traced.
audit_findings.action: Trace the $356m FY2025 and $150m YTD 2026 pension amounts through the OE worksheet; remove expected asset returns, actuarial amortization and $62m FY2025 settlement effects, then add only separately supported recurring cash pension contributions or receipts and rerun all scenarios.

audit_findings.title: The anchor mixes material transitory gains and charges
audit_findings.magnitude: FY2025: $184m gains, $167m LHX NeXt costs, $82m divestiture losses, $85m impairment and $57m transaction expenses; YTD 2026: $50m gains, $10m divestiture loss and $40m transaction expenses
audit_findings.mechanism: Unnormalized gains raise OE, while completed transformation costs, transaction costs, divestiture losses and impairments reduce net-income-based OE; perpetuating either side distorts operating and terminal value.
audit_findings.evidence: G&A expenses decreased $138 million, or 4%, for fiscal 2025 compared with fiscal 2024 primarily due to an increase in gains recognized in connection with the monetization of certain legacy end-of-life assets, lower LHX NeXt implementation costs, including lower third-party consulting expenses of $59 million, lower amortization of acquisition-related intangibles and merger, acquisition, and divestiture-related expenses, partially offset by an increase in business divestiture-related losses.
audit_findings.explanation: The transitory items are demonstrated, but the supplied record does not show their line-by-line treatment in the $2,399.6m anchor. The disclosed YTD 2026 gain and identified losses arithmetically offset before tax, while FY2025 identified charges exceed gains; unrelated items cannot be assumed to offset economically or recur together. Materiality and net direction therefore remain unresolved rather than disproven.
audit_findings.action: Reconcile the anchor to filed net income and cash flow line by line, identify every included gain and charge, normalize each independently with tax effects, and rerun the scenarios using the resulting recurring OE.

audit_findings.title: Accrued tax exposures may be an unmodeled senior cash claim
audit_findings.magnitude: $882m gross, comprising $754m unrecognized tax benefits and $128m accrued interest and penalties; $4.65 per share and 2.5% of $35,236m base equity value
audit_findings.mechanism: Any settlement not already captured in forecast cash taxes is a senior cash outflow that should reduce the equity bridge or future OE.
audit_findings.evidence: Unrecognized tax benefits, together with the related accrued interest and penalties, are presented within the “Other non-current liabilities” line item in our Consolidated Balance Sheet.
audit_findings.explanation: The omission is unresolved because gross accruals are not equivalent to expected cash settlement and may be reduced by offsets, deductions, favorable resolutions or statutes of limitation. Nevertheless, even deducting the entire filed $882m gross amount would reduce base value by only $4.65 per share, versus the $70.60 gap between the $185.85 base value and $256.45 market price. It therefore cannot change the stated valuation conclusion on the supplied numbers.
audit_findings.action: Obtain the expected cash-settlement schedule net of offsets and amounts already included in forecast taxes; deduct any residual claim in a bridge sensitivity and confirm no double count.

audit_findings.title: Future lease burden is absent from the current earnings anchor
audit_findings.magnitude: $1.1bn filed undiscounted future payments, including approximately $700m for the Camden facility
audit_findings.mechanism: Rent from leases commencing in 2026-2028 will reduce future OE, while the associated production capacity may create incremental revenue and require additional maintenance investment.
audit_findings.evidence: On January 2, 2026, we had additional future payments of $ 1.1 billion related to leases that have not yet commenced.
audit_findings.explanation: The commitments are documented but had not commenced and therefore were not expenses in the current anchor. They are forward-looking rather than a demonstrated error in historical OE. The $1.1bn is an undiscounted payment total over 7-20 years, not a present valuation loss, and the record does not quantify the incremental economics enabled by the facilities. Direction is consequently mixed.
audit_findings.action: Monitor commencement and utilization, then model annual rent, maintenance capital and supported incremental OE for each facility; rerun if the net economics are absent from the growth forecast or if a lease liability is later deducted separately.
